title: James Watt
summary: Born in Greenock in 1736, Watt worked as mathematical instrument maker to the University of Glasgow. In 1765, strolling on Glasgow Green, he devised a separate condenser that made steam engines far more fuel-efficient, and patented it in 1769. In 1774 he moved to Birmingham to partner Matthew Boulton at Soho. He died at Heathfield in 1819.
